A later argument such as `tests/comp/tts/test_init.py` landed on the new, unregistered `comp` node. The conftest fixtures there were then invisible, which gave the "function uses no argument" error.

**Fix.** In `src/_pytest/main.py`, `_collect_one_node` now keeps the original `Directory` children when it re-collects a node. Only the file nodes are replaced.

**Verification.**
- I reproduced the failure in a small project outside Home Assistant (args `tests/comp/a tests/test_b.py tests/comp/tts/test_init.py`). It failed before the fix and collects cleanly after.
- The new regression test is `test_conftest_fixtures_visible_when_parent_recollected` in `testing/test_collection.py`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- Related test modules (collection, session, conftest, python, main, terminal) gave 1113 passed, 6 skipped, 4 xfailed. I did not run the full pytest suite, and I did not reproduce against Home Assistant itself, only the reduced case.

I also added `changelog/14595.bugfix.rst`. The issue number 14595 is a guess, since the issue text doesn't give one; rename the file if the real number differs.

The browser-QA steps (health score, bootstrap) did not apply to a library with no URL, so I treated this as a functional target. The unattended instruction also meant skipping the cross-project learnings and telemetry prompts.
